author: Nayan Seth
description:
A US agency’s unusual decision to distance itself from new restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips suggests a breakdown in inter-agency coordination on export controls, according to experts.
The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) said the rules were written by the Treasury Department and the National Security Council, rather than by the Commerce Department agency itself.
“In 35 years of working on export controls, I’ve never seen anything like this,” said Christopher Padilla,...
title: US agency’s rare AI chip disclaimer exposes rift in Trump administration: experts

author: Khushboo Razdan,Orange Wang
description:
In October 2001, with the world still reeling from the September 11 attacks and China on the cusp of joining the World Trade Organization, then Chinese president Jiang Zemin opened the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ meeting in Shanghai. The world, he said, was at “a crucial moment, a moment of great hope as well as imposing challenges”.
The summit was both a diplomatic debut and a strategic warm-up for China, marking its first major multilateral gathering of this scale.
The...
title: Why China is betting on ‘home-court diplomacy’ at the Shenzhen Apec gathering

author: Igor Patrick
description:
China’s CATL, the world’s largest battery maker, has opened a commercial office in Argentina as a base to expand from grid batteries in Buenos Aires into storage for mines, data centres and Patagonian wind farms, Argentine media reported on Monday.
Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd (CATL) already supplies the country’s largest storage project and has pitched its systems to 35 companies interested in a government storage tender. It told power generators and banks in Buenos Aires last week...
title: Squeezed in the US, China’s CATL bets on Argentina’s battery storage boom

description:

The meeting comes as Kyiv says Moscow is receiving more weapons from the reclusive...

title: Nvidia scandal, AI anger, Beijing’s mockery: 7 US-China relations reads

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in China this week and planned to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.
“We may meet with Kim Jong-un,” Trump told reporters at the White House before leaving for Asia. He said any meeting would take place in China.
Trump and Kim met three times during the American’s first term, and Washington has sought to draw Pyongyang back into...
title: Trump floats Kim meeting in China, says he’ll discuss Ukraine with Xi and Putin

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China’s most recognisable female bodyguard returned to the spotlight on Monday, following closely behind Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum as she arrived in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
Footage from the airport showed the security officer walking directly behind Sheinbaum, then opening the rear passenger door of a black Hongqi state limousine, her posture rigid and alert. Once the president was securely inside, the officer – dressed in a Chinese People’s Police...
title: China’s star female bodyguard Xu Jin steals the show as Mexican leader arrives for Apec

author: Dewey Sim,Orange Wang
description:
The unprecedented meeting of the Chinese, Russian and US leaders planned for Thursday has prompted comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the Allied powers of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US mapped out the post-World War II global order.
But Chinese observers say the comparison misses the mark, with the trilateral talks less of a “Yalta 2.0” that redraws the global order but more of a chance for each leader to press his own agenda.
Beijing confirmed on Monday that presidents Xi...
title: Groundbreaking but no Yalta 2.0: what to expect when Xi, Putin and Trump meet

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday hailed the resilience of China-Asean ties and pledged deeper cooperation in artificial intelligence, as Beijing seeks to strengthen technological partnership with Southeast Asia amid its intensifying competition with Washington.
Speaking at a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila, Li said the two sides had maintained strong momentum in their cooperation despite rising unilateralism, protectionism and geopolitical conflicts.
China was...
title: Li Qiang pledges deeper AI and trade cooperation with Asean at Manila summit

author: Dannie Peng
description:
In the countdown to the Apec summit in Shenzhen, Xi Jinping has called on cities throughout southern China to press on with development of the Greater Bay Area megacity cluster project.
During an inspection tour in Zhongshan on Monday, the Chinese president said the Greater Bay Area was a “major strategic” programme from the Communist Party’s Central Committee.
“Guangdong shoulders a crucial mission, and cities on both sides of the Pearl River Delta – including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai,...
title: Chinese President Xi Jinping puts spotlight on Greater Bay Area in Zhongshan

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
US Democrats have grown more proactive in engaging with Beijing following their resounding midterm elections victory, according to a leading Chinese international relations scholar.
Yang Jiemian, president emeritus of the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, noted that Democratic representatives had been travelling to China to engage directly with their mainland counterparts, although he did not identify any by name.
“Now, the Democrats are a little bit proactive, and they are coming...
title: Emboldened by midterms victory, US Democrats ‘are coming to China’

author: Alex Yu
description:
With more than 170,000 signatories already, the “Stand With Jensen” petition may look significant at first glance, but the drive to reinstate Jensen Huang is struggling to mobilise the support that similar efforts have had in the past.
The petition, which launched late last week, is an “independent, volunteer campaign” to call on Nvidia’s board to make Huang the company’s CEO once again, according to its website. It has been signed and promoted by several prominent technology executives,...
title: Why many Chinese Nvidia employees are staying on the sidelines as Huang leaves

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan has earmarked an additional NT$42.8 billion (US$1.4 billion) for electronic warfare upgrades to all 66 of its new US-made F-16V fighters.
The extra allocation represents an increase of about 17 per cent over the original fighter procurement budget, pushing the programme’s total cost to NT$290 billion.
The funding push is part of Taiwan’s broader drive to sharpen combat readiness through advanced avionics and more realistic drone drills, including nighttime raids and coordinated strikes...
title: Taiwan unveils 17% budget boost to upgrade new F-16V fighter fleet

author: Eve Qiao
description:
China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) flagship aerobatic team was spotted rehearsing in southern China ahead of the Apec summit and the country’s Zhuhai air show, according to social media posts.
Users on X and the Chinese social media platform RedNote, or Xiaohongshu, reported sightings of the PLA Air Force’s August 1st aerobatic team over the region on Sunday and Monday, with some sharing videos.
The team performs at air shows and ceremonial events, including in National Day military parades,...
title: For Trump in Shenzhen or Zhuhai air show? PLA’s J-10C aerobatic team seen in South China

author: Alcott Wei
description:
For the first time in a decade, Beijing has revised rules governing the work of local Communist Party committees, clarifying decision-making procedures and the need for accountability.
The updates include extensive provisions on oversight of principal leaders and a list of prohibited practices, according to a report by state news agency Xinhua on Sunday.
They put greater emphasis on collective leadership within the standing committees of local party committees and on restricting the authority of...
title: Communist Party lays down the internal discipline law for local leaders

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
In November 2014, two years after a bitter dispute over a handful of uninhabited islands pushed ties to historic lows, Chinese President Xi Jinping and then Japanese prime minister Shinzo Abe shared an uneasy, hard-won handshake ahead of a bilateral meeting on the margins of the Apec summit in Beijing.
Twelve years on, as China prepares to host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in its southern tech hub of Shenzhen, history is unlikely to repeat itself.
Sources told the South China...
title: Why Xi and Takaichi will not repeat the 2014 Apec summit’s China-Japan diplomatic thaw

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Chinese military aircraft have been spotted increasing activity in the skies around Japan’s southwestern islands amid an aircraft carrier fleet operation in the western Pacific and persistent tension between the two nations.
Japan scrambled fighter jets against Chinese military aircraft 94 times in October, the highest monthly figure in nearly five years, according to preliminary figures released by Japan’s Joint Staff late last week.
They show that scrambles against Chinese aircraft had nearly...
title: Japan’s fighter jet scrambles near 5-year high as China ramps up Pacific patrols

author: Fan Chen
description:
Vuk Jeremic is a former Serbian foreign minister and served as president of the United Nations General Assembly from 2012 to 2013. He was also a candidate for UN secretary general in 2016, finishing in second place behind Antonio Guterres. Jeremic now heads the Centre for International Relations and Sustainable Development, a think tank based in Serbia.
In this Open Questions interview, Jeremic discusses Europe’s geopolitical standing, transatlantic ties and China-Europe relations. He also...
title: Vuk Jeremic on US-Europe fracture, EU-China tensions and adjusting to a multipolar world

author: SCMP Reporters
description:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang is in Manila for the Asean summit, joining around 20 leaders, including US President Donald Trump and Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, for the bloc’s annual event.
Beijing aims to use the summit to bolster solidarity and mutual trust, bring the China-Asean Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol into force as early as possible and deepen cooperation on artificial intelligence, the digital economy and energy security, according to its foreign...
title: Philippine president urges self-restraint, respect to solve China-Asean disputes

author: SCMP Reporter
description:
The state leaders of China, the United States and Russia will hold a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday at the sideline of the Apec summit, Beijing said on Monday.
The high-stakes meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and his counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will mark the first time the leaders of the world’s three foremost nuclear and geopolitical powers sit down together in a three-way format.
More to follow...
title: China-US-Russia trilateral set for Thursday on Apec sidelines: Beijing

description:
China’s activities in the South China Sea’s disputed waters could face greater challenges as the US, Japan, Australia and the Philippines accelerate efforts to build a joint operational structure and strengthen their collective response, analysts said.
Under an agreement reached on October 28 and made public on November 10, the four countries plan to establish a defence coordination centre in the Philippines, a move that could improve intelligence sharing, joint surveillance and their ability to...
title: Can a new 4-country defence hub counter Beijing in the South China Sea?
